release:
The XPath parser and tokenizer have changed beyond all recognition in the 25 years since they were first forked from James Clark's xt implementation. The open-source license terms relating to these components have therefore been removed.
Line numbering of XML documents read using a SAX parser (including schema documents and stylesheets) has changed.
Wherever possible, the line and column number associated with a node are now the position where the node starts: in the case of elements, the start of the start tag. Previously, Saxon reported the location returned by the SAX parser, which is the position after the associated SAX event (for elements, the end of the start tag). There are a few cases where this information is not available, notably when an element is immediately preceded by a DOCTYPE declaration or an external entity reference. In these cases Saxon will continue to report the location as reported by the SAX parser.
In addition, the linked tree model now retains line and column position for text nodes (if line numbering is enabled, which is always the case for stylesheets and schema documents). This enables more accurate location information to be provided for expressions in XSLT text value templates.
This change affects the line and column numbers reported by the saxon:line-number() and saxon:column-number() extension functions, as well as diagnostic output including the results of schema validation, the output of -T tracing, and so on.
The implementation of xs:duration and xs:dayTimeDuration has changed so the seconds component (representing the number of days, hours, minutes, and seconds) is now held internally as a BigDecimal value. This affects the range of values and precision that can be maintained (both are now essentially unlimited), and prevents arithmetic exceptions when manipulating extremely large or small values. The change also affects the internal APIs for constructing and manipulating instances of these two types.
The months component is unaffected: the total number of months in a duration remains limited to 2^31.
-->
The value returned from the function call system-property('xsl:vendor-url') has been changed from "http://www.saxonica.com/" to "https://www.saxonica.com/".
Some new convenience methods have been introduced for the XdmValue and XdmStream classes. In both cases, you can now write select("name") or select("uri", "local") as a shorthand for select(Steps.child("name")) or select(Steps.child("uri", "local") respectively. For example, the expression doc.select(Steps.child("test-set").then(Steps.child("dependencies"))).first() reduces to doc.select("test-set").select("dependencies").first().
The interface net.sf.saxon.s9api.StaticError, which was no longer used, has now been dropped from the product.
New methods checkpoint() and recover() have been added to the TraceListener interface. The default implementations do nothing. These methods are called when dynamic errors are caught using try/catch; in the case of the standard -T output, they are used to ensure that the trace output remains well-formed when errors are caught and recovered.
Add information regarding schema processing....
The classes ProfessionalXPathFactory and EnterpriseXPathFactory are dropped. It seems there were no tests referencing these classes, and JAXP XPath has gradually been deprecated. Need to drop the mention in the XPath documentation.
The internal APIs for manipulating values of type xs:duration and xs:dayTimeDuration have changed, reflecting the fact that the seconds component is now held as a BigDecimal value.
Some deprecated methods associated with handling of xsl:message output have been removed: in class XsltController, methods setMessageFactory(), setMessageReceiverClassName(), setMessageReceiver(), makeMessageReceiver(), setMessageEmitter(), getMessageEmitter().
The adaptive output method now does (fairly crude) indentation of maps and arrays if the indent serialization option is set. Previously maps and arrays were output without indentation.
The Transform command acquires a new option -stublib:filename. This is intended primarily for use when compiling stylesheets to SEF files for execution under SaxonJS. It allows a file of stub function definitions to be loaded in JSON format, representing external Javascript functions that will be available for calling in the target environment. Any attempt to call the functions from SaxonJ itself will fail with a dynamic error.
New features from the 4.0 specifications
Filter expressions accept a sequence of integer positions, for example $in[3 to 5] or $in[1, 4, 7].
The precedence of the otherwise operator has changed. The expression @price otherwise @cost * 2 now parses as @price otherwise (@cost * 2), not as (@price otherwise @cost) * 2.
In XPath, the for and let expressions now accept a larger subset of XQuery FLWOR syntax. Specifically:
Both for and let allow an as clause to declare the variable's type.
The for expression allows an at clause to declare a position variable.
for and let clauses can be mixed without an intervening return, for example for $x in $X let $y := $x + 1 return f($y).
Both XQuery and XPath now allow the syntax for key $k $value $v in $map to iterate over the entries in a map.
Choice item types are implemented, for example the required type of a parameter in a function signature can be (map(*) | array(*)). The local union type syntax union(xs:integer, xs:string) (which only allowed unions of atomic types) is dropped.
Variadic functions (syntax declare %variadic function) are implemented in XQuery.
The second $position argument is available on function callbacks made by the functions every, filter, for-each, index-of, some.
The functions starts-with-sequence, ends-with-sequence, contains-sequence are renamed starts-with-subsequence, ends-with-subsequence, contains-subsequence.
The functions deep-equal, distinct-values, duplicate-values, all-equal, all-different, starts-with-subsequence, ends-with-subsequence, contains-subsequence, now use transitive equality semantics: this means that numeric values of different types (for example xs:double and xs:decimal are compared by converting both values to decimals, not to doubles.
The deep-equal function now supports the items-equal callback. The collation and options arguments of deep-equal have been combined.
The function fn:format-number can now take an options map as the third argument.
The functions fn:min and fn:max now return one of the items from the input sequence as is, rather than converting it to xs:double.
The functions fn:seconds, fn:subsequence-where, fn:take-while, and fn-unix-dateTime are implemented.
The function fn:iterate-while is renamed fn:while-do, and the function fn:do-until is implemented.
The function fn:round acquires a third argument that can be used to control the rounding mode.
The functions map:values and array:values are implemented.
The functions map:empty and map:keys-where are implemented.
The function map:build allows multiple index entries to be created for a single input item.
The functions fn:csv-to-arrays, fn:parse-csv, and fn:csv-to-xml are implemented.
The function fn:compare, previously used only to compare strings, is extended to compare any comparable atomic values.
The new function fn:sort-with is implemented.
The new function fn:collation is implemented.
The new function fn:graphemes is implemented.
The new function fn:function-annotations is implemented.
The function fn:codepoints-to-string is now variadic: you can write codepoints-to-string(13, 10) instead of codepoints-to-string((13, 10)).
The functions fn:parse-xml and fn:parse-xml-fragment now accept an options parameter.
The deep-lookup operator ?? is implemented.
Comments (between '#' characters) are allowed in regular expressions if the 'c' flag is set. A '#' character can be escaped as \# or [#].
The fn:parse-json and fn:json-doc functions accept an option to allow JSON null to be represented by something other than an empty sequence, for example map{'null':[]} maps null to an empty array while map{'null':[]}.
The function fn:load-xquery-module accepts a new option content whose value is the text of the module to be loaded, as a string. This works whether or not 4.0 is enabled.
The rules for the number-parser callback in fn:parse-json and fn:json-doc have been changed to reflect changes in the specification.
In decimal format properties, it is now possible to set composite values for some properties, for example percent="%:pc" indicates that the single character "%" will be used in the picture string, but the value "pc" will appear in the output.
The functions math:e, math:sinh, math:cosh, and math:tanh are implemented.
The JSON serializer recognises the xs:QName value fn:null as a representation of the JSON null value.
The implementation of enumeration types has been aligned with the current specification. Most practical use cases are unaffected, but:
Casting a string to an enumeration type is now allowed.
The test "A" instance of enum("A", "B") now returns false; for an instance of test to work, the string must be converted to the enumeration type; this can be done with an explicit cast, or it can be done implicitly by applying the coercion rules.
The ItemType syntax union(a, b) has been dropped from the 4.0 specification, but remains supported in Saxon for the time being. The replacement syntax is (a|b) (the parentheses are mandatory). This allows, for example, as="(map(*)|array(*))" for a function or variable that accepts either a map or an array.
The adaptive serialization method has changed to output maps as {...} rather than map{...}.
Dropped experimental features
Some proposed enhancements that didn't survive into the current 4.0 draft specifications have been dropped:
The ternary conditional expression test ?? A !! B.
Record tests using the keyword "tuple" rather than "record".
Lambda expressions of the form ($a, $b) -> {$a + $b}
The syntax type(T) is now allowed only in XSLT patterns, not as an item type in XPath expressions. T may be any item type, including the name of a type alias.
The "thin arrow" notation for inline functions (->{.+1} or ->($x){$x+1}).
fn:all is renamed fn:every.
Saxon's experimental operators andAlso and orElse are dropped. The 4.0 specification defines and and or to have short-cut semantics, so these operators are unnecessary.
Local union types have been generalized to choice types; the syntax union(xs:int, xs:long) now becomes (xs:int | xs:long), and unions of other types are allowed (for example (map(*) | array(*)).
Some Saxon extension functions that were essentially prototypes of near-identical XPath 4.0 functions are dropped:
saxon:index-where is superseded by fn:index-where.
saxon:highest and saxon:lowest are superseded by fn:highest and fn:lowest.
saxon:is-NaN is superseded by fn:is-NaN.
saxon:parse-html is superseded by fn:parse-html.
A new vendor option has been added to the fn:transform function. Setting the option saxon:write-result-documents to true() changes the way the output of xsl:result-document instructions is handled. Instead of being returned in the result map returned by fn:transform, they are handled by the result document handler registered with the primary transformation, or the default result document handler otherwise: this has the effect of writing the secondary results directly to filestore.
The class XQueryFunctionLibrary, which holds details of all the functions in an XQuery module, has been redesigned to make importing of large XQuery modules more efficient. The function index is now organized first by namespace and then by local name, and uses immutable maps, so that importing a namespace now typically just adds a reference to the relevant imported module, rather than copying, revalidating, and re-indexing all the imported functions. This is particularly useful when a query module holding many functions is separately compiled and then used repeatedly in many different main modules. It provides savings both in compile time and in the size of XQuery executables.
